_meta.indication: Treatment of non-central nervous system manifestations of alpha-mannosidosis in adult and pediatric patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (3:2), double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group trial evaluating LAMZEDE 1 mg/kg IV weekly over 52 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive adult and pediatric patients aged 6-35 years with alpha-mannosidosis (25 total; by age: 13 adult, 12 pediatric).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The trial assessed two primary endpoints: change from baseline in serum oligosaccharide levels (a biomarker) and change from baseline in the 3-minute stair climbing test (3MSCT), assessed at 12 months; key secondary endpoints were the 6MWT and FVC % predicted.
pivotal_trials.result: 3MSCT mean relative change +0.5% (LAMZEDE) vs -3.6% (placebo), treatment difference 3.4% (95% CI -9.5, 16.3); FVC % predicted absolute change +8.2 vs +2.0, difference 5.5 (95% CI -5.0, 16.1); serum oligosaccharides relative change -75.8% vs -20.3%, difference -55.6% (95% CI -69.3, -41.9).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >20%) are hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, nasopharyngitis (66% vs 70% placebo), pyrexia (40% vs 50%), headache (33% vs 30%), and arthralgia (20% vs 10%). In clinical trials 19 (50%) LAMZEDE-treated patients experienced hypersensitivity reactions, including 2 (5%) with anaphylaxis.
target_moa: Velmanase alfa is a recombinant human lysosomal alpha-mannosidase that functions as enzyme replacement therapy; it is internalized by cells and transported to lysosomes where it catalyzes degradation of accumulated mannose-containing oligosaccharides that are deficient in alpha-mannosidosis.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human lysosomal alpha-mannosidase enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SEVERE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS. Patients treated with LAMZEDE have experienced hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis; if a severe reaction occurs, discontinue LAMZEDE immediately and initiate appropriate medical treatment.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Advisory Committee Summary was Not Applicable.

summary.text: LAMZEDE (velmanase alfa-tycv) was approved via the traditional approval pathway under a Priority Review as an enzyme replacement therapy for alpha-mannosidosis. It held Orphan Drug designation (granted February 2, 2006), Rare Pediatric Disease designation (granted December 11, 2018), and Fast Track designation (granted December 12, 2019). Efficacy was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial (rhLAMAN-05) plus confirmatory mechanistic evidence.

citations.quote: This application met the criteria for a priority review because velmanase treats a serious condition for which there is currently no approved treatment, and if approved, would provide a significant improvement in effectiveness in treatment of AM.
Velmanase received orphan designation in February 2006, rare pediatric designation in December 2018, and Fast Track Designation in December 2019.
A Rare Pediatric Disease designation was granted for velmanase on December 11, 2018.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness for velmanase alfa in AM patients was established with one adequate and well-controlled trial with confirmatory evidence.
